guarantees.claim: When in StIdle, if arb_valid is true, next state becomes StAppCfg and set_appid is asserted; if sw_cmd_i equals CmdStart, next state becomes StSw and cmd_o is set to CmdStart; otherwise next state remains StIdle.

In StAppCfg, if the selected app mode is AppKMAC and entropy_ready_i is false (mubi false strict), next state becomes StError and service_rejected_error_set is asserted; otherwise next state becomes StAppMsg and cmd_o is set to CmdStart.

In StAppMsg, mux_sel is driven to SelApp; when the selected app's valid and ready are both high and last is asserted, next state becomes StAppOutLen if mode is AppKMAC, otherwise StAppProcess; otherwise next state remains StAppMsg.
In StAppOutLen, mux_sel is SelOutLen and next state transitions to StAppProcess when both kmac_valid_o and kmac_ready_i are high.
In StAppProcess, cmd_o is driven to CmdProcess and next state unconditionally becomes StAppWait.
In StAppWait, if absorbed_i is true (mubi true strict), next state becomes StIdle, cmd_o is set to CmdDone, and clr_appid is asserted; otherwise next state stays StAppWait.
In StSw, mux_sel is SelSw, cmd_o follows sw_cmd_i, absorbed_o tracks absorbed_i; if sw_cmd_i equals CmdDone, next state returns to StIdle, else stays in StSw.
In StKeyMgrErrKeyNotValid, the FSM unconditionally sets next state to StError, asserts fsm_err.valid, sets fsm_err.code to ErrKeyNotValid, and stores app_id in fsm_err.info.
In StTerminalError, the FSM remains in StTerminalError, asserts sparse_fsm_error_o to 1, and sets fsm_err to valid=1, code=ErrFatalError, info=app_id.
When the current state does not match any explicit case (default branch), next state is forced to StTerminalError and sparse_fsm_error_o is asserted to 1.
If lc_escalate_en_i is asserted (loose test true), next state is unconditionally overridden to StTerminalError, regardless of prior st_d value.
When the next state is not StTerminalError and keymgr_key_used is true but keymgr_key_i.valid is false, next state is overridden to StKeyMgrErrKeyNotValid.

In StError, fsm_data_ready is set to the inverse of err_during_sw_q, and transition logic uses a unique case on {err_processed_i, (app_i[app_id].valid && app_i[app_id].last) || err_during_sw_q}: branches handle error processing and app draining, conditionally asserting fsm_digest_done_d, driving cmd_o to CmdProcess, and moving to StErrorServiceRejected, StErrorAwaitSw, StErrorAwaitApp, or StErrorWaitAbsorbed; a default branch keeps next state as StError.
In StErrorAwaitSw, if err_processed_i is true, cmd_o is driven to CmdProcess and next state becomes StErrorWaitAbsorbed.
In StErrorAwaitApp, fsm_data_ready is forced to 1; when the app valid and last are both true, fsm_digest_done_d is asserted, cmd_o becomes CmdProcess, and next state moves to StErrorWaitAbsorbed.

In StErrorWaitAbsorbed, when absorbed_i is true (mubi true strict), clr_appid is asserted, clear_after_error_o is set to MuBi4True, service_rejected_error_clr is asserted, cmd_o becomes CmdDone, next state returns to StIdle; additionally, if err_during_sw_q is true, absorbed_o is set to MuBi4True.
In StErrorServiceRejected, clr_appid is asserted, clear_after_error_o is set to MuBi4True, service_rejected_error_clr is asserted, and next state becomes StIdle without issuing CmdDone.

assumptions.claim: Input signal arb_valid must be stable and correctly indicate a valid arbitration request when asserted; the FSM relies on it to start app configuration.
assumptions.cond: st == StIdle and a new transaction begins
assumptions.risk: A glitch on arb_valid could cause an unintended transition to StAppCfg, setting app_id prematurely or starting an unauthorized KMAC operation.

assumptions.claim: entropy_ready_i must be a stable multi-bit mubi signal; its mubi4_test_false_strict test is used to reject KMAC mode if entropy is not ready. A metastable or surprising value could invert the check.
assumptions.risk: A corrupted mubi could misclassify entropy readiness, either blocking a valid KMAC operation or allowing one without entropy, potentially weakening key material.

assumptions.claim: App interface handshake (app_i[app_id].valid, app_o[app_id].ready) must follow a valid/ready protocol and last signal must be asserted only for the final data beat; the FSM uses these to drain messages during error recovery.
assumptions.cond: st is StAppMsg, StError, StErrorAwaitApp, or related error drain states
assumptions.risk: Protocol violations or deadlocks on the handshake could trap the FSM in an absorbing/draining state, blocking error recovery and potentially leaking or stalling key operations.

assumptions.claim: err_processed_i must be asserted by software only after the error condition has been fully handled; the FSM waits for this signal in StError and StErrorAwaitSw before proceeding to flush.
assumptions.risk: If err_processed_i is asserted prematurely, the FSM may proceed to flush before the error is fully contained, potentially allowing a compromised digest or key exposure.

assumptions.claim: keymgr_key_i.valid must be a faithful indicator that the key manager key is usable; the FSM checks this only when keymgr_key_used is active and st_d is not terminal, otherwise proceeds.
assumptions.risk: A false valid signal could allow a KMAC operation with an invalid key, compromising key-dependent operations. A false invalid signal could needlessly abort a valid request.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case in the main FSM (561-563) drives st_d to StTerminalError and sets sparse_fsm_error_o to 1, but does not set fsm_err.valid or fsm_err.code. In the same cycle, the fsm_err output defaults to valid=0, ErrNone. If an illegal state is entered, the error output may not be signalled until the next cycle, and the error code is not set.
uncertain_points.risk: The system may not immediately recognize a fatal illegal state transition, potentially executing one additional cycle with corrupted state before terminal error handling is visible, weakening fault containment.

uncertain_points.claim: Lifecycle escalation (570-572) overrides st_d to StTerminalError but does not set sparse_fsm_error_o or fsm_err in the same combinational cycle; these signals are only driven in the StTerminalError case when the current state is already StTerminalError. If the current state is not StTerminalError, the escalation results in a one-cycle delay before fsm_err is asserted.
uncertain_points.risk: A critical system escalation may be delayed by one clock cycle in terms of visible error signalling, potentially allowing a secret-bearing operation to progress briefly under extreme fault conditions.

uncertain_points.claim: In StErrorWaitAbsorbed (539), absorbed_o is set to MuBi4True only when err_during_sw_q is true, indicating to software that the operation was absorbed even though an error occurred. The intent of reporting 'absorbed' after a SW error versus after an app error may be inconsistent or could mislead higher software layers.
uncertain_points.risk: If software interprets absorbed_o as successful completion, a subsequent action might rely on a corrupted or invalid digest, potentially breaking security protocols that expect error indication instead of absorption.

uncertain_points.claim: In the StError state unique case (463-501), the concatenated select signal is formed by {err_processed_i, (app_i[app_id].valid && last) || err_during_sw_q}. If any component becomes X (unknown) due to a fault, the case expression may also become X, and the default branch will keep the FSM in StError indefinitely with no immediate error escalation.
uncertain_points.cond: st == StError and any of err_processed_i, app signals, or err_during_sw_q is X
uncertain_points.risk: An undetected fault could hang the FSM in StError, blocking recovery and all further operations, without asserting a terminal error or logging a unique fault code.
